timeline.message:
Fix correct enrich cache bug.

The enrich cache currently uses `SearchResponse` as cache value,
which contains the hits used by the enrich processor for enrichment.
What is actually used is by the enrich processor is `SearchHit.getSourceAsMap()`,
which is a map of maps representation of a search hit.

The problem is that this map is mutable and the map of maps is directly
passed into `IngestDocument` and at the same time this is cached by the
enrich cache via `SearchResponse` cache value. Any processor that modifies
the content added by the enrich processor, also changes the map of maps
representation of a search hit in the cache. This corrupts the cache,
because if this the enrich cache serves a cache entry for the same key,
a different snippet added to the document being enriched.

The following changes have been made to fix this bug:
* Use `List<Map<?, ?>>` as cache value for the enrich cache.
* Upon caching lookup / search, make an immutable deep copy of `SearchHit.getSourceAsMap()`.
* Upon serving an entry from the cache, make a normal deep copy,
  so the enrichent can be safely modified by subsequent processors.

Closes #82340
timeline.author: Martijn van Groningen

timeline.body:
The enrich cache currently uses `SearchResponse` as cache value,
which contains the hits used by the enrich processor for enrichment.
What is actually used is by the enrich processor is `SearchHit.getSourceAsMap()`,
which is a map of maps representation of a search hit.

The problem is that this map is mutable and the map of maps is directly
passed into `IngestDocument` and at the same time this is cached by the
enrich cache via `SearchResponse` cache value. Any processor that modifies
the content added by the enrich processor, also changes the map of maps
representation of a search hit in the cache. This corrupts the cache,
because if this the enrich cache serves a cache entry for the same key,
a different snippet added to the document being enriched.

The following changes have been made to fix this bug:
* Use `List<Map<?, ?>>` as cache value for the enrich cache.
* Upon caching lookup / search, make an immutable deep copy of `SearchHit.getSourceAsMap()`.
* Upon serving an entry from the cache, make a normal deep copy,
  so the enrichent can be safely modified by subsequent processors.

Closes #82340

I was thinking, maybe we store the enrich hits as byte[]? And then upon retrieval we parse it into `List<Map<?, ?>>`. 

We already do some work here just before storing a cache entry (recursively make an immutable copy of the search hits (just to catch anyone trying to corrupt the cache) ) and when serving from this cache (recursively make a mutable copy of the search hits). 

I think if we cache the byte[] representation of search hits we save some heap space. At the cost of some additional operations when serving from cache or adding a new entry to cache. But that should be ok, since we already do some extra work making deep copies.

reply.body: It is hard to guess for me what the right tradeoff is in terms of the cache size vs compute cost here. Bute note, even a deep copy will be far cheaper than deserialisation that's for sure. I think instinctively I'd rather go for a deep copy because that saves memory after retrieval because all the strings (at least the map keys) will be shared instead of recreated on parsing over and over.
I see, this makes sense. Let's stick with creating a deep copy each time an entry from the cache is used.

timeline.body: I'm not as familiar with all the data types that may be present in the map from a `SearchHit`, but `IngestDocument::deepCopy` handles a couple types that this method does not. ([link](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/master/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/ingest/IngestDocument.java#L742))

reply.body:
Initially I looked at the `IngestDocument#deepCopy(...)`  method, but then realised that some of the data type (e.g. `Set`, `long[]`, `Date`) are never in the search hit. The `SearchHit.getSourceAsMap()` method uses `XContentHelper#convertToMap(...)` method, which eventually invokes `AbstractXContentParser#readValueUnsafe(...)` via `XContentParser#map()` method and I think the mentioned types are never produced by the `readValueUnsafe()` method.

I think we can reuse `IngestDocument#deepCopy(...)`. There is some code duplication between the two methods. But this method will then need to be modified to optionally wrap list / map in an unmodifiable wrapper and this would only be used by `EnrichCache`. I currently lean towards keeping this method, since the code duplication is minimal and it is targeted for creating a deep copy of search hits. But if we keep this method then we need a good unit test for it as well. What do you think?

timeline.body: LGTM. Left one non-blocking comment below that might not be relevant for search hits.
